subject: SOC 2 evidence & cloud carve-out — mapping and bridge letter request
messages:
From: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@skybank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 16:21:00 -0000
Subject: SOC 2 evidence request and cloud carve-out clarifications

Hi Connor —

Thanks for taking this. We're running SkyBank's annual vendor SOC 2 intake and have a couple of targeted asks for Redwood to close our review for the payments team. Attached is our short questionnaire (SkyBank_Security_Q4_2027.pdf). High-level asks:

- SOC 2 Type II report covering period Nov 1, 2026 — Oct 31, 2027 (or an equivalent bridge letter if coverage dates differ).
- Confirmation of any carve-outs in Redwood's SOC 2 related to cloud provider responsibilities (GCP/AWS). If Redwood relies on provider SOC reports for controls, we need either:
  - copy of the provider SOC 2 + explicit mapping showing which controls are covered by the provider, or
  - a bridge letter from Redwood clarifying the shared responsibility surface and any gaps.
- Current subprocessor inventory and whether key services (KMS, object storage, logging) are included in the report scope.
- Evidence of encryption key custody (KMS ownership/keys-in-customer-control vs. provider-managed).

Can you share the above by EOD next Tuesday (Nov 16)? If you need a narrower ask list we can prioritize, but we need confirmation before procurement signs off on the SOW.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Rachel
Rachel Stone
Senior Information Security Manager, Third-Party Risk
SkyBank

Attachments: SkyBank_Security_Q4_2027.pdf
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@skybank.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 09:34:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request and cloud carve-out clarifications

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the clear ask list. Quick summary / next steps from our side:

1) SOC 2 Type II: attaching our latest report (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf). The audit period on the report is 2026-11-01 through 2027-10-31.
2) Subprocessors: attaching current inventory (subprocessors_inventory_2027.csv). That file includes cloud providers (GCP, AWS), KMS providers, and a note on whether a processor is in-scope for SOC.
3) Cloud carve-out: Redwood's SOC 2 does rely on cloud provider SOC coverage for some infrastructure controls. We do not automatically include provider reports in our PDF; instead we provide a mapping table that aligns provider controls to Redwood controls. I will coordinate with Cloud Security to produce that mapping and confirm whether we can provide copies of the underlying provider reports.
4) KMS custody: for customer keys we support both customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations) and Redwood-managed keys. The inventory file includes the default custody model per service. If SkyBank requires a specific custody model for production, let us know and we can flag it on the procurement SOW.

Attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf, subprocessors_inventory_2027.csv

Can we schedule a quick 30-min sync on Monday (Nov 15) for mapping and bridge-letter expectations? I'll pull in Cloud Security (marissa) and our GRC contact.

Thanks,
Connor
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0148
From: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@skybank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Adam Willis <adam.willis@skybank.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 13:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request and cloud carve-out clarifications

Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — that helps. A few follow-ups after reviewing the SOC and the inventory:

- Audit period: the audit period on your SOC aligns to our requirement (good). We still need a written confirmation (bridge letter) that maps provider coverage for the controls listed in sections CC6 and CC7 (infrastructure availability and encryption/key management). Specifically, we need to see which controls are satisfied by GCP/AWS SOC and which are Redwood's operational controls.
- Provider reports: we prefer vendor-supplied copies of provider SOCs where possible (e.g., GCP SOC 2). If you cannot provide the full provider PDF due to contract restrictions, the mapping + a Redwood attestation will suffice.
- KMS: we see Redwood supports customer-managed keys on certain services. Please confirm the specific service names that can be BYOK and whether BYOK is available in the Dedicated offering.
- Evidence examples: if you can provide a short evidence packet for one control (e.g., CC7.1 encryption at rest key management for object storage) — such as a screenshot of key policy, a log extract, or a short runbook — that would expedite review. A redacted audit trail is acceptable.

Proposed timeline:
- Nov 16: proposed mapping table + confirmation on BYOK availability
- Nov 18: draft bridge letter (if required) and a one-control evidence packet

If that timeline doesn't work on your side, let us know the earliest you can provide the mapping and sample evidence.

Best,
Rachel

Hi Rachel —

Looping in Cloud Security ownership. Quick answers and owners: 

- BYOK availability: Confirmed for object storage and KMS-backed secrets in Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted (shared) offering, BYOK is available for select enterprise customers via our KMS integration layer — procurement needs to set up a key escrow relationship. Owner: cloudsecurity@redwood.com (cloudsec lead: S. Nguyen).
- Provider SOCs and mapping: We will produce a mapping table that aligns AWS/GCP SOC controls to Redwood controls and indicate where we rely on provider coverage. If the provider contract permits, we'll attach provider SOC PDFs. Owner: Marissa (cloud GRC).
- Bridge letter: Attached is a short draft bridge letter (proposed_bridge_draft_2027.docx) that covers the audit window you requested (2026-11-01 through 2027-10-31) and calls out the specific provider responsibilities and compensation actions if provider coverage changes mid-window. We can tailor the language to SkyBank's procurement template.
- Evidence packet: We can prepare a redacted evidence bundle for CC7.1 (encryption at rest / key management) by Nov 18.

We're happy to join the Monday sync to finalize the mapping and confirm any redaction needs.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Cloud Security - GRC, Redwood Inference
